Vorinel was a craftsman from Sunstrider Isle. He survived the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas and reached The Bazaar in Silvermoon City, the only section of the capital the elves had reclaimed from the Scourge. He questioned Kael'thas Sunstrider's silence after the prince's arrival, but later concurred with his plan to destroy the tainted Sunwell. Cosmic is a school of magic. It is a multi-school that combines , , , and . Many Devourer demon hunter abilities use it, as does the Fatebound hero talent tree for rogues. Shade salmon were an extinct species of fish native to Shadowmoon Valley on Draenor, notable for being touched by void magic. Considered a delicacy by the Shadowmoon clan, it was important for them to only be eaten directly after being freshly caught, as their magical properties caused their meat to become toxic after prolonged exposure to sunlight. The Azerothian Southfury Salmon is said to have a similar flavor.

Shattered Devastators are centurions found at the Font of Fealty in the Spires of Ascension during the Oryphrion encounter on Mythic difficulty. They are inactive and unattackable at first. When Oryphrion recharges its anima, any Shattered Devastators that have an Anima Field underneath them will become active and attackable.

The Forgotten Experiments is a boss in Aberrus, the Shadowed Crucible. It consists of three individuals created by Neltharion 20,000 years ago, during his attempts to create the dracthyr. Neldris was the fourth created, and closely resembles a black drakonid but lacked the desired arcane strength. After it is Thadrion, the 147th experiment, which appears as a heavily-mutated drakonid. It was imbued with excess arcane power, which led to unstable and undesired magical surges. The final is the 328th experiment Rionthus, created by refined infusion processes and appearing as an arcane-imbued dracthyr. Each was deemed unsuccessful and put into stasis, as they were found too dangerous to destroy.

Combat Intelligence is a game mechanic for XCOM 2 added in the War of the Chosen DLC. It determines how quickly soldiers earn Ability Points in combat, allowing them to purchase abilities that would normally need to be chosen through promotion. A soldier's Combat Intelligence can be improved through specific Covert Actions. When this is done, Ability Points match the new Combat Intelligence, meaning it will retroactively gain the ability points they would have gotten at that level when gaining points in the field.

Dustwallow Marsh (or Dustwallow Swamp) is a vast and ancient swamp in the eastern reaches of Central Kalimdor. Although there is little activity in the area, the Alliance and the Horde have recently expanded their influence in the region. The Alliance city-state of Theramore was located on a small island east off shore but was eventually destroyed by a mana bomb ordered by the then-Warchief Garrosh Hellscream. The Horde major stronghold in the area is Brackenwall Village, the new home of the ogre Stonemaul clan.

Duskwither Spire is a floating tower located in northeastern Eversong Woods. It has been overtaken by arcane creatures and Wretched. It was once a magical academy run by Magister Duskwither, but fell into disrepair after the magister began looking into ill-fated ways to solve his race's addiction to magic. Adventurers are asked to deactivate the power sources there by Apprentice Loralthalis.

Empowered Frostbolt is a mage talent that increases Frostbolt's spell power bonus by 5/10%, and reduces its cast time by 0.1/0.2 sec. Frostbolt normally has a spell damage bonus of 81.4% of total Frost spell damage. The bonus from the talent is additive, with rank 2 Empowered Frostbolt increasing the spell damage bonus to 91.4%. The critical strike chance is additive as well, and only applies to the Frostbolt spell.

Empowered Rejuvenation is a Druid talent in the Restoration tree. You will need to spend 40 points in Restoration to max it. This talent increases the spell power coefficients of your heal over time spells, increasing how much they benefit from your spell power, by up to 20% at max rank. The talent affects Lifebloom, Rejuvenation, Regrowth, Tranquility, and Wild Growth.

Energy is the primary resource used by rogues, druids in Cat Form and Brewmaster and Windwalker monks. Energy regenerates at a fixed rate of 1 energy every decisecond (i.e. every one tenth of a second), in and out of combat, and is under most circumstances capped at 100. This makes energy a very fast-regenerating and fast-depletable resource. Certain energy-using rotations may benefit from energy pooling to maximize efficiency. Many abilities using Energy have a fixed Cooldown#Global cooldown (GCD) of 1.0 seconds that is not affected by haste.

The fal'dorei are a race of former elves found in Suramar. Many years ago, exiles from Suramar City came to Falanaar. Valewalker Farodin took pity on them and gifted them with an arcan'dor tree. For a time it sustained them and they were safe, but it did not last forever. The arcan'dor became unstable and died, and in a flash of wild magic the elves were twisted into spider-like creatures, becoming the fal'dorei. Now they live in the tunnels beneath Falanaar and were after the arcan'dor seed protected by Farodin. The fal'dorei intended to use its power to return to the surface. Fel-corrupted fal'dorei can be found in the Cathedral of Eternal Night, in the service of an aranasi, Nal'asha.

__NOTOC__ Falanaar (or the Ruins of Falanaar) is a small ruined town behind Ambervale in Suramar that was heavily damaged in the Sundering, the destruction of the Tidestone of Golganneth, the loss of the first Arcan'dor, or some combination thereof. Based on the wall around the town, it does not appear to be a former part of Suramar City. The ruined Temple of Fal'adora, dedicated to Elune, is located here. Part of the town has collapsed into the Falanaar Tunnels where the Fal'dorei reside. Between the tunnels and the temple is the Shattered Locus, a failed arcan'dor. Moonshade Sanctum is nearby.

The Farstriders are an order of elite blood elf rangers, once high elf, active in Quel'Thalas. They are led by the Ranger-General of Silvermoon, Halduron Brightwing, who succeeded Sylvanas Windrunner after the Third War. The Farstriders are based in Silvermoon City, but they have several camps and lodges scattered all across Quel'Thalas. They are considered part of the blood elf government. Intimately bound to the wildlands, and with a deep respect for the law, the rangers that compose the Farstriders' ranks remain noble, traditional, and valiant protectors of blood elf society.

Faronaar is a large island found in western Azsuna, covered in the ruins of a majestic city that used to be on the road to the Well of Eternity and Zin-Azshari. The island is heavily controlled by the Burning Legion.
Farah Skybeak is a Highmountain tauren flight master for Skyhorn in Highmountain.

Fate's End is an uninhabited island off the western coast of Stormsong Valley. A few runed pillars, Drust ruins, can be found on its southern coast, while a few wrecks mar the northern coast. Only the tidesages can safely access the island, for it is a place where the seas froth and the air cracks with thunder. Kul Tirans tried settling Fate's End once, but each settlement disappeared into this mist, every soul never to be seen again. Now the island is used as a place to exile the worst criminals, but people who are exiled to Fate's End never return. It is somehow connected to Thros, which is where the missing exiles are dragged into.

Fated Power: Protoform Barrier is one of the fated powers applied to a raid boss during a Fated Raid. It causes Protoform Barriers to summon that empower the raid boss and once removed it, because an hostile shield that starts counting down for 15 seconds. Upon expiration, it'll explode and inflict Cosmic damage to all players. If players break it before the timer runs out, it instead inflicts the damage to each enemy during the barrier encounter and all players are given a 40 second buff that increases damage, absorbs and healing by 20% and health by 30%.

Fated Power: Reconfiguration Emitter is one of the fated powers applied to a raid boss during a Fated Raid. It creates a Reconfiguration Emitter which starts casting spells at all players, which inflicts Cosmic damage. Every five seconds, it gains increased damage, which stacks. It cannot be attacked until the first successful cast or an interrupt, which will inflict a smaller amount of Cosmic damage to all players. Upon defeat, all players gain power based on the energy level of the emitter and increasing mastery by up to 10, critical strike and versatility by up to 10%, and avoidance by up to 9.
Fel Turkey! is a dungeon & raids achievement earned by destroying 30 Infernal Spikes with Shattering Stars and then defeating Goroth in Tomb of Sargeras.

Felhounds (also known as fel hounds, felbeasts, felhunters, hellhounds, manastalkers, fel demons and fel stalkers) are red, wolf-like creatures with no eyes and spined mane originating from the depths of the Twisting Nether. Felhounds are demon hounds used by the pit lords to sniff out sources of magic wherever they be found. Felhounds, who feed upon magic itself, are fond of draining the energies of hapless wizards and then ripping their bodies to shreds. Each has two tendrils, ending in a sucker of sorts, which they use to drain their prey's power and, eventually, their life. They serve as the forerunners of the Burning Legion.
Felinni is a panther and is one of many animals featured in the Darkmoon Faire zoo on Darkmoon Island. Felinni shares a spawn location within the same corral as Lizzy.

Felsiege Infernals are infernals located in Snowblind Mesa in Highmountain, Old Coast Path in Azsuna, and near Bradensbrook in Val'sharah during Legion Assaults. They also appear on the Broken Shore as well as in Shattered Fields in Krokuun and at the Shattered Chasm in Antoran Wastes on Argus.

Feral attack power was an attribute specific to feral druids. Only druids could see the stat, displayed as orange text, in the tooltip of weapons. No weapon had a specific bonus to feral attack power; rather, all weapons with more than 54.8 DPS contained the appropriate amount of feral attack power. It was removed in Patch 4.0.1.

Feltotem Caverns is a large cavern on the Misty Coast near Feltotem in western Highmountain. It used to be a settlement of a group of neutral drogbar, but they were pushed out by concerted demon and fel tauren attacks. The Feltotem tribe was breeding fel infused worms in here in order to destroy Thunder Totem. During the course of the third invasion, Navarrogg and the adventurers entered the caverns to disrupt the breeding operations by destroying eggs and killing the Fel Broodmaster. This place was also used by the demons to give instructions to the Feltotem.

Field Commander Romus is a human quest giver located at Honor Hold in Hellfire Peninsula. With his arrival, he inspired draenei in their efforts to militarize their old ruins from Hellfire to Shattrath City. Romus tasked Alliance adventurers with killing Shattered Hand elites of the Fel Horde inside Shattered Halls. After Kargath's death, Force Commander Danath Trollbane wanted to speak with Romus about following up and ensuring that the orcs stayed on the defensive.
Festival Talespinner can be found in Undercity, Orgrimmar, Thunder Bluff, Silvermoon City, during the Midsummer Fire Festival.

A fiery destroyer can consume a dead creature but it provokes attacks of opportunity. The destroyer cannot consume dead creatures that were immune to fire in life.

Fire Jugglers are first encountered by players at the Darkmoon Faire portal in either Elwynn Forest or Mulgore, depending on your faction. Once in Darkmoon Island, they can be found throughout the Faire itself, entertaining guests by tossing fiery torches to one another.
__NOTOC__ Fiora Moonsoar is a night elf flight master found at Mirkfallon Post within the Stonetalon Mountains.

:Were you looking for the tauren quest giver ? The Firemane are a group of dragonkin belonging to the black dragonflight. They reside in and around Onyxia's Lair in Dustwallow Marsh. You can also see some flying high above Alcaz Island.

The Firebrand Legion is a division of Rend Blackhand’s Blackrock orcs that reside primarily in the lower levels of Blackrock Spire. This legion are mainly made up of spellcasters that call on the power of flame. In fact, the Firebrand Darkweavers and Dreadweavers have the ability of cursing their enemies with their legion's curse: Curse of the Firebrand, a fire-based curse. All of them cast Mark of Flames, which is a magic debuff that increases the fire damage taken by an enemy by 1000 for 2 minutes. Bannok Grimaxe is a member of the Firebrand Legion.

Fizzcrank Airstrip is a gnome base in northern Borean Tundra, which overlooks the Geyser Fields and its pools of stinking, boiling water. The airstrip rings with the sounds of hammer on anvil morning through night, though half the time you can barely hear them over the gnomish flying machines taking off. A hydrothermal system underlies the area around the airstrip, which connects it to the geyser fields to the southeast, where the gnomes built the Fizzcrank Pumping Station, an oil platform used to make fuel for their flying machines, until the mechagnomes took control of it. Several gnomish bombers and flying machines are stationed there.

First Squadron Prototypes are bombers used by the Gnomish Elite Aerial Rangers during the Heritage of Gnomeregan questline. They represent the latest innovations in flying machine technology and are powered by a Prototype Arcane Engine. Two prototypes are first seen at the Fizzcrank Airstrip in the Borean Tundra for A Tundra Conundrum. During Now With More Mechanical Fowl, the G.E.A.R. Commander is tasked with calibrating one of the the bombers' prototype guns by using it against the Ironbound threatening the airstrip. The Flame of Silvermoon is obtained when an Alliance character clicks on the Midsummer Flame in Silvermoon City.

Flamestar Post is located immediately south of the bridge leading to Blackrock Mountain in the Burning Steppes. It is a small camp run by the Thorium Brotherhood and serves as the first quest hub for those entering the Burning Steppes. While here, adventurers help start a plan to fight back against the Blackrock orcs. It contains a flight path and an Adventure Board leading Horde players into Blackrock Depths.

Fleeting Wind is a conduit for death knights. It drops from Kin-Tara in the Spires of Ascension, Sire Denathrius in Castle Nathria, and the Tarragrue in the Sanctum of Domination. An ilvl 145 version is also rewarded from Strengthen the Bond, A Journey Made Together, Strengthening the Bond (Night Fae), and Strengthening the Bond (Venthyr).
Flight Form (aka The Raven or Storm crow) is a Druid ability that is learned after training Expert Riding. This form is only usable in areas where flying is allowed and unlocked.
Flik's Frog is a frog found with Flik at the Darkmoon Faire on Darkmoon Island.

Flight School: Flapping Frenzy is one of the three Flight School world quests in Bastion required for the achievement Flight School Graduate. After completing the world quest normally, Malo offers a paragon difficulty, which has much tighter tolerances. Should players complete it, they will be awarded the extra achievement Aerial Ace.

Flow of Time is a conduit for mages. It drops from the Stone Legion Generals in Castle Nathria and Soulrender Dormazain in the Sanctum of Domination. An ilvl 145 version is also rewarded from Strengthen the Bond, A Journey Made Together, Strengthening the Bond (Night Fae), and Strengthening the Bond (Venthyr).
Flightstones introduces players to Flightstones, the Dragonflight Season 2 item upgrade currency.
Flying High is an achievement awarded for flying through 10 rings in one flight session of the Firebird's Challenge event. See the linked article for details and tactics.
